newsitem.title: USA: Protesters disrupt New Hampshire wood chip factory.
newsitem.headline: Protesters disrupt New Hampshire wood chip factory.

text.p: New Hampshire state and local police Monday dispersed two dozen environmental demonstrators at a wood processing plant near the Maine border and arrested one man who was chained to a chipping machine.

Members of the environmental group Native Forest Network descended on the wood chipping plant, operated by the Mead Corp., shortly after 5 a.m. and occupied the site in Shelburne, N.H., about 50 miles south of the Canadian border.

"We went on the log piles and occupied those so they would not be moved. We then blocked the wood scales at the entrance, and one person locked themselves on the chipper," Native Forest Network spokesman David Pike said. Pike said timber companies were harvesting too many trees in the White Mountains National Forest, causing environmental damage.

The activists hung up up banners that read, "Native Forests Not Chips" and "Any Fool Can Destroy Trees." Police arrested one man on trespassing charges. Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
